newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD sees 76 pct profit rise-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD sees 76 pct profit rise-paper.

text.p: Soon-to-be privatized state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) has achieved a 76-percent profit increase in 1996 in inflation adjusted terms to 632 million reais ($607.69 million), a newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil said this was the company's third best result after 1988 and 1994 when inflation-adjusted net profit amounted to $730 million and $645 million, respectively.

CVRD Director Anastacio Fernandes Filho attributed the profit increase to a six-percent rise in international iron ore prices, the firm's cost reduction program and tax exemptions on exports, Gazeta said.
The company sold a total of 103.16 million tonnes of iron ore and pellets in 1996.

Under Brazilian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), CVRD's 1996 net profit rose 57.62 percent to 517 million reais ($497.1 million) from 328 million reais ($315.4 million) in 1995, Gazeta said.
CVRD is expected to be privatized in April with the initial sale of a 40 to 45-percent block of voting shares, followed by staff and global offers later in the year.
The final tender details and possibly the minimum price for the block sale are due to be announced today.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
